summary: Robert Caro discusses his interpretation of Robert Moses and Lyndon Johnson: how they accumulated leverage, overcame opposition and changed as they acquired power. He also explains his interviewing, archival research and writing methods, including defining a book's central point before drafting and the limits of faster document discovery. This is the Caro interview itself, distinct from Patel's preceding video essay. The full publisher transcript includes the opening, all eleven chapter sections and closing thanks; sponsor copy and trailing site material were excluded from the assessment.
why_it_matters: Useful background on institutions, infrastructure politics and evidence collection. The discussion does not provide a concrete new AI, technology-company, semiconductor or compute-infrastructure finding. Applying Caro's historical interpretations to present-day firms or data-center projects would require additional evidence.
